free_tier.stated: 100 trillion bytes (~100 TB) of data storage awarded across the programme each year; per-project archival quota at OLCF is 200 TB (shared across Project/World/User Archive on Kronos).

retention.stated: Tenured infrastructure; data survives, but the allocation expires and the archival quota can be clawed back after project end - treat as renewable-while-funded, not permanent.

egress.terms: Globus/GridFTP and SSH transfer free to allocation holders; no egress meter. Data is not a public HTTP origin.

record.tooling: SSH/scp/sftp, Globus, Lustre + HPSS/Kronos nearline mounts; no S3.
record.chaining: One allocation = one project directory on a 100+ PB Lustre (Eagle/Orion) plus up to 200 TB nearline archive. Storage is not separately metered, so a storage-heavy proposal can request a large quota against a small compute request - but the proposal must still justify compute.
record.limits_note: Annual call only (mid-April to mid/late June), awards 1-3 years with a peer-reviewed annual renewal request. Post-project archival storage is explicitly at the facility's discretion ('The facilities reserve the right to limit the amount and duration of archival storage once a project has been completed'). Data must be research data.

record.notes: Two review phases: an international peer-review panel on scientific merit, then a technical assessment of computational readiness by LCF staff. Requests under 20% of the average award are redirected to Director's Discretionary or ALCC. Early Career Track reserves 10% of allocatable time for PIs within 10 years of a PhD who have not previously been INCITE PI. Polaris is no longer available; Aurora and Frontier are the only INCITE resources for 2027. The 20% utilisation criterion is the real filter at this scale: a solo researcher must show the campaign consumes a fifth of an exascale machine. Node-hour to GPU-hour conversion depends on the system (Frontier nodes carry 4 MI300A APUs), so earlier readings should not convert without a per-system figure.
